newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka to try 11 soldiers, police in rape case.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka to try 11 soldiers, police in rape case.

text.p: Eleven soldiers and policemen are being held in a Sri Lankan jail in connection with the rape and murder of a teenaged Tamil girl and the killing of three other people, court officials said on Monday.

Four army privates and two reserve police constables are accused of raping and killing Krishanthi Kumaraswamy and killing her mother, brother and a neighbour who went looking for the missing girl in September.
The five other suspects helped dispose of the bodies in a salt pit, the defence ministry said.

Colombo chief magistrate Munidasa Nanayakkara ruled on Monday that the trial of the 11 would take place in two weeks in northern Jaffna, the former Tamil rebel stronghold where the crime was committed.
A group of about 100 women's rights activists demonstrated outside the court, demanding an impartial inquiry into the killings, punishment for the accused and compensation for victims' families.
The group said in a statement that the case was not an isolated one and that previous offenders had escaped while the victims were denied justice.

The crime was believed to have been committed when the accused manned a checkpoint set up to prevent infiltration by Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam rebels, who are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war, now in its 14th year.
